- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.22 or lower) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next few days — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and smooth downward slope.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment > 0.05.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.10), model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- In early 2024 (e.g., Feb 2024), model shows persistent underestimation of volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–15% for high-sentiment periods.
